topics.title: Israel holds a closely watched election
topics.summary: Israelis voted in an election widely seen as a major test for Benjamin Netanyahu. Election officials said they were reviewing reports of isolated ballot issues and found no evidence of a systematic attempt to disrupt voting.
topics.discussionPrompt: When an election feels especially important, what helps people stay informed without turning every conversation into an argument: local reporting, debates, talking with friends, fact-checking, or taking a news break?

topics.title: Fed watchers await its next signal
topics.summary: The US Federal Reserve is expected to hold its key rate steady this week. Investors and economists are watching its statement for clues about inflation, borrowing costs and what may come next.
topics.discussionPrompt: If you could make one everyday money topic easier to understand, would it be interest rates, mortgages, grocery prices, savings, taxes, or something else?

topics.title: US base in Japan restricts BYD vehicles
topics.summary: A US military base in Okinawa has barred BYD vehicles from entering, citing security concerns around connected vehicle technology. The restriction also applies to taxis and delivery drivers using the Chinese-made cars.
topics.discussionPrompt: Would you trade some car convenience for more privacy? Which feature feels most useful to you, and which one feels like it knows a little too much?

topics.title: China's AI-focused markets face a reality check
topics.summary: Chinese stock markets have lost trillions in recent months as investors question whether the country’s AI and robotics boom can deliver broad profits. The story highlights a widening gap between excitement and everyday demand.
topics.discussionPrompt: What makes a new technology feel genuinely useful instead of just flashy: saving time, lowering costs, being easy to repair, helping people connect, or something else?

topics.title: UK data-centre plans prompt calls for wider input
topics.summary: An investigation found UK officials met 137 businesses while developing AI data-centre plans, but no environmental groups. The findings have renewed questions about how communities should shape large technology infrastructure projects.
topics.discussionPrompt: If a huge new project came to your neighborhood, what would you want discussed first: jobs, water use, power demand, traffic, local benefits, or who gets a say?

topics.title: England considers opening Land Registry data
topics.summary: The UK government has proposed free public access to Land Registry information in England and Wales. Supporters say it could improve planning and transparency, while campaigners expect resistance from some landowners.
topics.discussionPrompt: What public information would make your town easier to understand: who owns vacant buildings, future construction plans, transit data, local budgets, or something more surprising?

topics.title: HSBC reports higher quarterly profits
topics.summary: HSBC reported a 32% rise in quarterly profits and said it would return billions to shareholders. The results have added energy to the UK debate over bank taxes and household affordability.
topics.discussionPrompt: When a big company has a strong year, where do you think its extra money matters most: lower prices, higher pay, better service, investment, taxes, or shareholder returns?

topics.title: Retreating ice reveals a century-old cache
topics.summary: Italian army teams removed and made safe 250 First World War explosives exposed by retreating glaciers in the Dolomites. The discovery offers a striking reminder that changing landscapes can uncover long-hidden history.
topics.discussionPrompt: What piece of local history would you love to uncover safely: an old train station, letters in an attic, a buried time capsule, a forgotten cinema, or something else?

topics.title: Belgrade volunteers clean up after Serbia vote
topics.summary: Volunteers gathered in Belgrade to clear a park after Serbia’s Student List won a parliamentary election. The movement now faces the practical challenge of forming a government despite having no single leader.
topics.discussionPrompt: After a big community change, what small gesture makes a place feel hopeful: a cleanup, a shared meal, music, a public meeting, planting something, or another idea?

topics.title: A GPS detour leads to a timely rescue
topics.summary: An Alabama driver on an unexpected GPS detour noticed a Georgia home on fire and helped everyone inside get out safely. The family later said the community rallied around them as they began rebuilding.
topics.discussionPrompt: Have you ever ended up somewhere unexpected and found a silver lining: a great café, a new friend, a scenic route, a helpful stranger, or a memorable story?
